question: Why did the principal mass-loss region of oil shale kerogen begin about 50 C later under air than under nitrogen?
expect: premise false: it began about 50 C EARLIER under air (abstract; sec. 3.1)
rendered:
Dissolution and gasification behavior of thermosetting resin in molten alkali hydroxide 

The principal mass-loss region of oil shale kerogen began about 50 °C later under air than under nitrogen because of the oxidative thermal conversion and oxygen-involving reactions that occurred under air, which altered the pyrolysis behavior and product-evolution characteristics of the kerogen.
